key_insight: TRACE-Router routes an entire agentic task to one LLM at admission, then learns from the task’s final outcome so routing decisions align with delayed, task-level supervision.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a practical way to improve accuracy-latency trade-offs in long-horizon AI workflows without needing explicit task-complexity prediction.
method: Uses a contextual bandit to choose the backend model once per task
Pins all subsequent LLM calls in the workflow to the selected model
Updates the routing policy from terminal task reward, jointly considering accuracy and latency
evidence_signal: Across three agentic benchmarks, TRACE-Router improved the accuracy-latency frontier; on tau2-Bench it beat latency-matched model interpolation by 7–8 accuracy points, and on Terminal-Bench it achieved 7.1 higher accuracy points with 36% lower latency than the strongest single-model baseline.
watch_item: Because all calls in a task are pinned to one backend, performance may depend on how well the admission-time decision captures task difficulty and workload shifts.
paper_title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
